## Story Goal

Deliver a shared library of pre-written reply templates that agents can search and pick from when composing ticket / chat replies:

1. A `QuickReply` document model with `title`, `category`, `body`, `createdBy`, timestamps.
2. A REST resource (`GET /list+search`, `GET /:id`, `POST`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`) with granular permissions:
   - **Read (list/search/get)**: any authenticated **agent** or **admin** (subadmin with `quickreplies:view`).
   - **Write (create/edit/delete)**: **admin-only** (implicit) or subadmin with the specific write permission — mirrors the split described in the intake.
3. An admin surface at `/admin/system-configuration/quick-replies` for CRUD, modelled on `/admin/ticket-categories`.
4. Four new permission keys wired into `backend/src/constants/permissions.ts` and `frontend/lib/permissions.ts`, plus staff-nav entry and i18n strings (en + ar).

**Explicitly out of scope for this story:**
- Tasks/reminders (Story 22), internal-team collaboration (Story 24), system-configuration umbrella UI (Story 47).

## Product rules (from story)

- **Read** (list, search by `q`, filter by `category`, get-by-id): any authenticated **agent** or **admin**, plus subadmin with `quickreplies:view`. Customers are **not** allowed.
- **Write** (create, edit, delete): admin implicit-pass; subadmin only via explicit `quickreplies:create` / `quickreplies:edit` / `quickreplies:delete`; agents are **denied**; customers are **denied**.
- Quick replies are organised by a free-form `category` string (no separate collection). List endpoint must support `?q=<title|body substring>&category=<exact>`.
- Titles can repeat within and across categories (no unique index).
- Selecting one on the client inserts the body into the reply textarea — **backend does not enforce this**; it just serves the data.

### 2 — Create the model

**Create file:** `backend/src/models/QuickReply.ts`

```ts
import mongoose, { Document, Schema, Types } from "mongoose";

export interface IQuickReply extends Document {
  title: string;
  category: string;
  body: string;
  createdBy: Types.ObjectId;
  createdAt: Date;
  updatedAt: Date;
}

export const QUICK_REPLY_TITLE_MAX_LENGTH = 120;
export const QUICK_REPLY_CATEGORY_MAX_LENGTH = 60;
export const QUICK_REPLY_BODY_MAX_LENGTH = 4000;

const quickReplySchema = new Schema<IQuickReply>(
  {
    title: { type: String, required: true, trim: true, maxlength: QUICK_REPLY_TITLE_MAX_LENGTH },
    category: { type: String, required: true, trim: true, maxlength: QUICK_REPLY_CATEGORY_MAX_LENGTH },
    body: { type: String, required: true, maxlength: QUICK_REPLY_BODY_MAX_LENGTH },
    createdBy: { type: Schema.Types.ObjectId, ref: "User", required: true },
  },
  { timestamps: true }
);

// Compound index to support the primary list query: category filter + title sort.
quickReplySchema.index({ category: 1, title: 1 });
// Text index to back the ?q= search across title + body.
quickReplySchema.index({ title: "text", body: "text" });

export const QuickReply = mongoose.model<IQuickReply>("QuickReply", quickReplySchema);
```

### 4 — Add the routes

**Create file:** `backend/src/routes/quickReply.routes.ts`

Copy the skeleton from `backend/src/routes/ticketCategory.routes.ts`. Key differences:

```ts
router.get(
  "/",
  requireAuth,
  requirePermission("quickreplies:view"),
  async (req, res) => {
    const parsed = listQuickRepliesQuerySchema.safeParse(req.query);
    if (!parsed.success) { res.status(400).json({ error: parsed.error.issues[0]?.message ?? "Invalid query" }); return; }
    const { q, category } = parsed.data;
    const filter: Record<string, unknown> = {};
    if (category) filter.category = category;
    if (q) filter.$or = [
      { title: { $regex: q, $options: "i" } },
      { body:  { $regex: q, $options: "i" } },
    ];
    const rows = await QuickReply.find(filter).sort({ category: 1, title: 1 }).limit(200);
    res.status(200).json(rows.map(toQuickReplyResponse));
  }
);

router.get("/:id", requireAuth, requirePermission("quickreplies:view"), /* 404 on invalid ObjectId; else fetch + toQuickReplyResponse */);

router.post("/", requireAuth, requirePermission("quickreplies:create"), validateBody(createQuickReplyBodySchema), /* create with createdBy = req.user!.id, 201 */);

router.patch("/:id", requireAuth, async (req, res) => {
  // Mirror ticketCategory.routes.ts:110–156:
  // 1) validate ObjectId → 404
  // 2) findById → 404
  // 3) safeParse update body → 400
  // 4) Per-field permission gate via callerHasPermission(req, "quickreplies:edit")
  //    — any field change requires that one key. Return 403 if missing.
  // 5) Apply fields, save, return toQuickReplyResponse.
});

router.delete("/:id", requireAuth, async (req, res) => {
  if (!(await callerHasPermission(req, "quickreplies:delete"))) { res.status(403).json({ error: "You do not have permission to perform this action" }); return; }
  // 404 handling as above, then QuickReply.deleteOne + 204.
});
```

Copy the `callerHasPermission` helper verbatim from `ticketCategory.routes.ts:53–56`. Do **not** import it — declare it locally (it references `req.user!`).

### 5 — Response shape

```ts
function toQuickReplyResponse(r: IQuickReply) {
  return {
    id: r.id,
    title: r.title,
    category: r.category,
    body: r.body,
    createdBy: r.createdBy.toString(),
    createdAt: r.createdAt,
    updatedAt: r.updatedAt,
  };
}
```

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Empty `q`** — treat missing and empty-string `q` identically (no `$or` filter added). Enforced in the list handler.
- **Very long `q`** — cap at 200 chars via `listQuickRepliesQuerySchema`. Reject with 400 otherwise.
- **Regex-special characters in `q`** — the list handler passes `q` straight into `$regex`; escape it first (e.g. `q.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, "\\$&")`) or the executor risks either a query error or ReDoS. **Do this** in the list handler.
- **Category with trailing/leading whitespace** — the model uses `trim: true`, but the list filter matches raw. Trim `category` in the query parser too.
- **Deleting a quick reply that no one is currently editing** — hard delete is fine; unlike categories, quick replies leave no snapshot on tickets/chats, so referential drift is a non-issue.
- **Agent tries to create/edit/delete** — 403 from `requirePermission` / `callerHasPermission`. Verify agents' default permission set (Task 1) does not include the write keys.
- **Deactivated staff user** — the `callerHasPermission` helper's `isActiveAccount` short-circuit catches deactivated admins (`[[feedback_permission_gating_audit]]`). The route-level `requirePermission` catches deactivated subadmins. Confirm both paths are covered by tests.
- **ObjectId validation on `/:id` routes** — `mongoose.isValidObjectId(req.params.id)` before `findById` (mirrors `ticketCategory.routes.ts:114`). Return 404, not 400, on malformed ids to match project convention.
- **Body over 4000 chars** — Zod rejects with 400.
- **Unicode / RTL in title, category, body** — no case-normalisation is needed (no unique index). Spot-check with an Arabic sample in tests.
- **Duplicate title in the same category** — allowed. Do **not** add a unique index. Document this in the model doc comment.

## Test Plan

1. **`backend/tests/routes/quickReply.routes.test.ts`** — new file, modelled on `backend/tests/routes/ticketCategory.routes.test.ts`. Cover:
   - GET `/` unauthenticated → 401.
   - GET `/` as customer → 403.
   - GET `/` as agent (with `quickreplies:view`) → 200, returns seeded rows.
   - GET `/?q=refund` filters on substring (title and body); GET `/?category=Billing` filters exact match; `?q=&category=` behaves like no-filter.
   - GET `/?q=` containing regex special chars (`.*`, `[`) does not throw.
   - GET `/:id` invalid ObjectId → 404; missing id → 404; found → 200.
   - POST as agent → 403; as admin → 201 with `createdBy = admin id`; as subadmin with `quickreplies:create` → 201.
   - POST with missing title → 400; body > 4000 chars → 400.
   - PATCH as admin edits title/category/body independently → 200; as subadmin with only `quickreplies:view` → 403; as subadmin with `quickreplies:edit` → 200.
   - DELETE as admin → 204; as agent → 403; on missing id → 404.
   - Deactivated admin token → 403 on both write and read (via `isActiveAccount`).
2. **`backend/tests/constants/permissions.test.ts`** — extend the existing key-set assertions to include the four new keys, and verify `SUBADMIN_ONLY_PERMISSIONS` includes the three write keys but not `quickreplies:view`.

## Migration / Rollback

- New collection only; no changes to existing collections. Rollback: drop the `quickreplies` collection and revert the four commits (permissions constants, model+routes, admin UI, i18n).
- No backfill needed. On a half-applied deploy (backend live, frontend not), the admin nav item won't appear yet — that is harmless. On the reverse (frontend live, backend not), the admin page will render an empty error state from the failing action — acceptable transient.
- The three write permission keys are additive; existing subadmins do **not** receive them retroactively. If the intent is for existing subadmins to gain them, add a one-off script under `backend/scripts/` (out of scope for this story unless the executor is told otherwise).
